notes:
I don't have any commentary notes on Jeremiah 27 for you yet, because none of my research worked.

I tried to fetch six pages in one go: Enduring Word's Jeremiah 27 page, Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary and Gill on BibleHub, the Precept Austin Jeremiah 27 page, and the NET Bible notes. A coding error stopped me from reading what came back. When I tried again to look at the results, the tool said I had no calls left for this turn. I never saw the content of any page, and I didn't get to search the other traditions or the Catholic and Orthodox sites.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and to give a URL for every point. If I wrote notes now, they would come from my memory, not the sources, so I haven't written any.

**Next steps:** if you reply (even just "continue"), I should be able to use the tools again. I'd then:
1. **Read the main verse-by-verse sources:** the six pages above, plus StudyLight if needed.
2. **Look for differences between Protestant traditions:** the Wesley Center (wesley.nnu.edu), Ligonier, Monergism, The Gospel Coalition, Desiring God, Grace to You, Spurgeon, the Lutheran sites (LCMS, 1517), and the Pentecostal and charismatic sites. Questions likely to come up are how Nebuchadnezzar can be "My servant" (v. 6), the length of the exile (v. 7), how to tell true prophets from false ones (vv. 9–18), and the temple articles being restored (v. 22).
3. **Gather the other views:** modern scholarship (NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey, for example on the different wording in the Septuagint), Catholic (newadvent.org, catholic.com) and Orthodox (oca.org). I'd also check whether any of the sites discuss popular modern teaching on this chapter.
4. **Write the notes verse by verse** ("v. 4: …"), with a URL after each point and nothing included that the pages don't support.
